previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, interstitial lung disease, diastolic heart failure, morbid obesity, and anticoagulation for prior pulmonary emboli was admitted for worsening dyspnea on exertion and suspected fluid overload. She had self-increased her torsemide dose prior to admission but remained short of breath. Evaluation revealed elevated troponin and CK, attributed to her underlying myositis rather than acute coronary syndrome. A CT scan ruled out pulmonary embolism but showed stable reticulonodular opacities consistent with interstitial lung disease. She was treated with IV diuresis, which was adjusted after an episode of intravascular depletion and acute kidney injury. Her INR became supratherapeutic, requiring vitamin K. Methylprednisolone was increased for a suspected polymyositis flare, and plans were made for outpatient rituximab. Due to deconditioning and new oxygen need, she was discharged to rehab with optimized heart failure and immunosuppressive therapy.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with morbid obesity, 
polymyositis complicated by interstitial lung disease, multiple 
PEs, DVTs, diastolic heart failure and pulmonary hypertension 
who presents with increased weight and worsening dyspnea in the 
setting of not taking her medications for ___ weeks.
 
# Acute on Chronic dCHF: Hx of worsening dyspnea, orthopnea and 
weight gain suggestive of CHF exacerbation. This is in the 
setting of medication noncompliance for ___ wks after wheelchair 
broke down and patient was not able to access her medications. 
BNP on admission was 34 although patient has had low BNP in past 
with prior CHF exacerbations, and obesity can lower BNP. 
Troponins negative x2. Per patient, her dry weight is between 
430-450 lbs. Given that she appeared fluid overloaded with 
increased weight on admission, she was diuresed with 100mg IV 
lasix twice daily with vigorous urine output. After improvement 
in her respiratory status back to baseline, she was transitioned 
to 100mg PO torsemide daily.  She was continued on metoprolol 
succinate 100mg daily. At the time of discharge, patient weighed 
211.8 kg.

# Weakness: Patient presented with weakness below her baseline, 
likely due to a combination of deconditioning due to immobility 
and worsening polymyositis due to stopping medications. Her AM 
cortisol was very low at 4, likely due to adreanl suppression 
from chronic steroid use. She was continued on 
methylprednisolone, mycophenolyate mofetil, and bactrim for 
prophylaxis. She was evaluated by physical therapy, and due to 
weakness and deconditioning, will be discharged to STR.

# multiple DVTs/PEs: Pt is on lifelong anticoagulation. Due to 
stopping warfarin for several weeks, INR was 1.0 on admission. 
Patient was started on a heparin bridge and warfarin. Her INR on 
day of discharge was 2.1. She was discharged on 6 mg daily. She 
should have her INR monitored closely after discharge until on a 
stable dose. 
 
# Diabetes:  Metformin held in house and patient maintained on 
insulin sliding scale. Pt was restarted on metformin at 
discharge.  

# Depression: continued citalopram.

# GERD: continued omeprazole.

# OSA: continued BiPAP w/ 4L nc.
 
# hypertension: continued metoprolol.

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
====================
# please check INR daily until on a stable regimen. warfarin 
dosing may need adjustment.
# please check electrolytes regularly until patient stabilized 
on PO diuretic regimen.
# monitor cardiopulmonary exam and volume status. diuretic 
dosing may need further titration
